implemented_requirements.evidence: config.py defines BEGINNER, INTERMEDIATE, EXPERT GameConfig objects and DIFFICULTY_LEVELS mapping; gui.py builds a difficulty menu from DIFFICULTY_LEVELS.
gui.py binds <Button-1> to on_left_click, which calls game.reveal_cell(row, col).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Numbers on uncovered cells indicate adjacent mines
implemented_requirements.evidence: game_logic.py calculates adjacent_mines in _calculate_adjacent_mines; gui.py draws the number with appropriate color when cell.is_revealed and cell.adjacent_mines > 0.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Uncovering a mine causes a loss
implemented_requirements.evidence: MinesweeperGame.reveal_cell sets state to STATE_LOST and marks the exploded mine when cell.is_mine is True; gui.py shows a dialog on STATE_LOST.
gui.py calls draw_board() after every reveal or flag action, redrawing all cells based on their current state.
MinesweeperGame.toggle_flag toggles Cell.is_flagged; gui.py binds <Button-3> (and <Button-2>) to on_right_click which calls toggle_flag.
gui.py uses FLAG_SYMBOL (⚑) and a unique background color (#FFD966) when cell.is_flagged is True.

judge.summary: The submitted code provides a complete, functional Minesweeper implementation with three preset difficulties, click‑to‑reveal, adjacent‑mine numbers, loss on mine, automatic board redraw, flagging, and a unique flag visual. All core requirements are met and the code appears ready to run.
